summary: Verified the search-count fix. Backend routes work individually but the new /api/wp/posts/count endpoint has a CRITICAL reliability bug: it lacks the retry/cache logic that wp_get() provides, so WP rate-limit/cold-start returns {"total":0}. Because the frontend only fetches the count once per query and uses `total && total > totalShown` to decide the label, a 0 makes the UI fall back to the OLD format 'X results for q' and the Load More button says 'Load more results' — exactly the user-reported symptom. Reproduced in browser (Direct fetch #1 -> 0, #2 -> 53; UI stuck showing '20 results for roth'). 6/7 backend tests pass; the failing test is the intermittent all-posts count (returned 0 then 196 on retry). Pagination, category filter, date ordering, and recent-2026 posts in results are all working as expected.

critical.issue: No retry and no cache. When WP returns 429 or any non-200 (very common on cold start), the handler silently returns {total:0}. This is the root cause of the user's original complaint — the fix is being defeated by an unreliable count call. Fix: route through wp_get() like /wp/posts does (with retry + short TTL cache) and parse X-WP-Total from the response headers, OR wrap the httpx call with the same 3-attempt retry loop used in wp_get and cache the result for ~60s. Reference: /app/backend/server.py:627-648

minor.issue: wp_get() caches X-WP-Total only in the response body — but the count route uses raw httpx and can't reuse wp_get()'s cache directly. Consider a helper wp_head(path, params) that returns headers with cache + retry.

ui_bugs.issue: Falls back to old '20 results for q' when postsCount returns 0. Not a bug in this file per se, but consider: when total<=totalShown and hasMore is also true, that's a paradox — could log/console.warn to catch future regressions. Reference: /app/frontend/app/search.tsx:192-196

Result cards don't render the post date. The review requested verifying 'at least one visible result has a 2026 date in its metadata' — the metadata currently shows only category + title + reading_time (line 217-225). Backend response includes p.date, but it's not rendered. Reference: /app/frontend/app/search.tsx:216-226

integration_issues.issue: api.postsCount fires once, silently swallows errors (`.catch(() => {})`), and never retries. Combined with backend returning 0 on 429, users see 'N results' + 'Load more results' — the exact pre-fix experience. Recommend either (a) backend retry/cache OR (b) frontend: if total===0 && results.length>=PER_PAGE, retry the count once after 1.5s. Reference: /app/frontend/app/search.tsx:42-46

action_items: PRIMARY FIX: Make /api/wp/posts/count reliable. Refactor to use retry (like wp_get) and a small 60-120s cache. Example: reuse wp_get by requesting per_page=1 and returning len; OR duplicate the retry loop and read X-WP-Total on 200. Right now every WP cold-start returns 0 and defeats the intended UX fix.

SECONDARY (optional but recommended): In search.tsx runSearch, if `total===0` but the results page came back full (raw.length >= PER_PAGE), retry api.postsCount once after ~1.5s so the label self-heals when backend cache warms.
OPTIONAL UI: Add the article date (e.g., 'Jan 12, 2026 · 6 min read') to search result cards so users can visually confirm recent posts appear (this was one of the user's original observations).

Re-test after fix: hit /api/wp/posts/count?search=roth 3 times in a row from a cold state; every response must be > 0. Then open /search, type 'roth', verify UI reads 'Showing 20 of 53 for roth' and Load More reads 'Load 20 more'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py wp_posts_count (line 627) duplicates the httpx client setup instead of reusing wp_get — this is why it's missing retry+cache. Encapsulate a shared helper (e.g., _wp_request that returns (body, headers)) and use it in both endpoints.
search.tsx line 44: silent `.catch(() => {})` on postsCount hides all errors — at minimum log to console in dev.

wp_posts_count returns 0 on error which is indistinguishable from 'legitimately zero results' — consider returning null/omitting field so frontend can show 'Showing 20 results' (no of-total) instead of the confusing fallback.

success_rate.backend: 86% (6/7 tests; the 1 failure is the exact bug reported)
success_rate.frontend: 60% (empty state, results list, pagination, category chip, clear button work; count label & load-more label do NOT match spec because backend returns 0)

context_for_next_testing_agent: The count endpoint is intermittent. To reproduce the bug: (1) wait 60+ seconds for backend cache to expire, (2) open /search, type 'roth', (3) observe count text says '20 results for roth' not 'Showing 20 of 53 for roth'. Direct API test: `curl /api/wp/posts/count?search=roth` — often returns {"total":0} on the first hit, {"total":53} on subsequent. Backend test file /app/backend/tests/test_iteration11_search_count.py already includes the coverage; the test_count_all_posts flake demonstrates the bug. After the fix, run: pytest /app/backend/tests/test_iteration11_search_count.py -v.
rca_of_issue: Original user report: 'search results only show a few posts and none recent'. Real cause: user was confused by the count label showing e.g. '20 results' when WP has 53. Applied fix added a /api/wp/posts/count endpoint + a 'Showing X of Y' label. However, the new endpoint uses raw httpx WITHOUT retry or cache, unlike wp_get(). When WordPress rate-limits (429) or cold-starts, it silently returns 0. Frontend then evaluates `0 && 0 > 20` = false and falls back to the OLD 'N results' text, defeating the fix. Reproduction: two consecutive curls to /api/wp/posts/count?search=roth returned 0, then 53. Fix: mirror wp_get's retry-and-cache behavior in the count endpoint (or delegate to wp_get and count the returned list via a dedicated helper that surfaces X-WP-Total).
